fix(cells)!: text is walked and edited one grapheme cluster at a time (rich-cells-1y9d) (#291)

* fix(cells): text is walked and edited one grapheme cluster at a time (rich-cells-1y9d)

Rule repeats its characters through setCellSize, so a glyph of several code
points is cropped whole, and refuses characters that take no cells.

TextInput moves, deletes, transposes and draws its cursor by grapheme cluster:
nextGrapheme/prevGrapheme replace the code-point steppers it was their only
caller of. Its printable gate measured UTF-16 length, so every astral code
point the router sends was dropped and no emoji could be typed at all.

A sweep test pushes ❤️, 👨‍👩‍👧, 🇺🇸 and a combining mark through every width walk
in cells.ts.

* fix(widgets): TextInput's cursor is a grapheme boundary whoever sets it (rich-cells-1y9d)

value and cursorPosition write through graphemeBoundary, so a replaced
value, a click, or an insert that grows the cluster before the cursor
cannot leave it inside a glyph or past the end. maxLength cuts between
glyphs; the password mask is one cell per glyph; Ctrl+T on one glyph is
a no-op.

* fix(widgets): an insert lands the cursor at its end; value holds line breaks as \n (rich-cells-1y9d)

The value setter had already moved the cursor past a cluster the insert
grew, so adding the insert's length on top overshot. CRLF and CR become
LF on write, as an HTML textarea's value does: \r\n is one cluster, and
a cursor could not rest at its line's end.

* fix(widgets): TextInput's cursor setter takes a CodeUnit; value writes are one action (rich-cells-1y9d)

An insert maxLength refuses whole emits nothing. C1 controls are not
text. The click hit-test reads the render's per-glyph projection
instead of a second copy of it.
